desc: Parse input: read N and the list P of length N from stdin.
Initialize a Fenwick tree of size N with all values 1 (all positions occupied), and an array `ans[1..N]` to record which original value sits at each final position.
Implement BIT operations: `add(i, delta)` for updates, `sum(i)` prefix sums, and `find_kth(k)` to locate the smallest index with prefix sum ≥ k (binary lifting, O(log N)).
Loop i from N down to 1: use `find_kth(P_i)` to get the position `pos` where value i ends up, set `ans[pos] = i`, then `add(pos, -1)` to remove it.
After the loop, join `ans[1..N]` with spaces and print to stdout.

Implement the complete Python solution: fast input parsing, O(N) Fenwick tree initialization, binary-lifting kth query, reverse loop assigning positions, and output — verified against the sample trace (Sample 1 → `4 2 3 1`, Sample 2 → `1 2 3 4 5`).
